mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (Rank IC < 0.10) or show a positive median return.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes or the effect is not robust across business cycle phases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime that erodes real corporate earnings and compresses valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 5-year averages
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (Rank IC < 0.05) or the effect reverses in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in housing starts (HOUST) combined with rising personal savings (RSAFS) signals a recovery in household balance sheets and pent-up demand, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both show 3-month positive momentum
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of concurrent HOUST and RSAFS momentum, or the effect is not present in more than 50% of episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 10-year average for three consecutive months signals a drawdown in household financial buffers, which increases marginal propensity to consume and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending rises.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of low RSAFS, or the effect is reversed during severe economic stress.
